objective: Backlog B144 (G1, question 9), at the owner's go-ahead of 2026-11-11, challenging A62 (a law gives a shape only by forcing it) and A63 (a named face is put in, not native). Worlds are finite sets of distinctions with three-place knots on them and nothing else: no board, no names, no declared faces. A uniform law puts one symmetric three-place knot on every knot of the world (parity, not-all-equal, the clause, or not-exactly-one, up to complement), with every distinction in d knots, and with or without the surface condition (each co-knotted pair in exactly two knots, each link one cycle). Frozen before any run on the test worlds: which worlds each law allows and keeps native (every knot a bond of the world's allowed states), whether its bonds of size three are exactly the world's knots with no ties (the world read faithfully from allowed states), what it fixes in every world it allows (finite lists at positive curvature, orientability, size), whether the surface condition follows from any law, and bond distance on small flat worlds. Standalone value relative to the nearest known work: the worlds and their curvature are classical (double counting, the regular triangulations, Altshuler's T(r,s,t), weak 2-colourings of triangulations, shatter complexes); what is new is reading them through the knot test, so that the shape is recovered, collapsed or spaced by the allowed states alone.
stop_rule: One epic: one frozen census and its checks; a stress test one size past. If no law reads flat worlds faithfully and composes, A63 stands for this setting; no further epic in the line without a new route named first.
title: Knots alone
